pnpm.//: React Native singletons. packages/ui-native declares these as peerDependencies "*" and is consumed as SOURCE, so pnpm's auto-install-peers gives it its own copy at the newest published version — Metro then bundles two Reanimateds and two gesture-handlers, which breaks module init for the whole app. Pinning here guarantees exactly one copy. Keep in step with apps/mobile.
pnpm.//react: React is the same kind of singleton, and it was silently broken until the admin console became the first Next app anyone ran. apps/mobile pinned react 19.2.3 while apps/web, apps/admin and packages/ui asked for 19.2.4; under node-linker=hoisted only one wins the root, and the result was react 19.2.3 hoisted next to react-dom 19.2.4 — a renderer mismatch that throws "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useInsertionEffect')" on the first render of any page. Pinned to 19.2.3 rather than 19.2.4 because react-native 0.85.3 peers react "^19.2.3": both satisfy it, but 19.2.3 is what the mobile app already runs, so this leaves the one shipped app untouched. Keep in step with apps/mobile.
